title: Sìleas nic Rath taken on as the chronicler's clerk
summary: Raghnall mac Mhuirich, keeper of the Library, finds the wage out of his own fund for binding and takes on Sìleas nic Rath, a copyist's niece of Àth dhìreach, as clerk to Seanchaidh na Rìoghachd. Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh had asked the council for a clerk three times and been refused or ignored each time.

title: The slip-box of the word's spellings
summary: At Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh's asking, Sìleas nic Rath begins a box of slips, one to a spelling, of every form the fuel's name takes in the letters that come up the library road: dubhan, dùbhan, dùban, and once, for a fortnight only, An Dubhan with the article and a capital letter.

title: The maor of Cathair mhòr's letter marked first
summary: The first letter marked in Sìleas nic Rath's box is the maor of Cathair mhòr's, which speaks of the fair price of dùban and says nothing of the man who first made it. Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh reads it for the clerk as the mark of a name going out of its own word.

title: The letter of Caol shean
summary: Scoiltean nan Draoidhean at Caol shean writes to Neach-gleidhidh an Leabharlainn of a word its masters have coined among themselves, dubhan-tùsail, for a first attempt that looked a failure and proved the one that held, offered for an Leabharlann's keeping though the school does not ask that it be used.

title: Dubhan-tùsail entered and never used
summary: Raghnall mac Mhuirich copies Scoiltean nan Draoidhean's coined word into an Leabharlann's word-list in his own hand, under the day's entry, and never uses it again in anything he writes that year. The word stands unused on the page, unstruck and unbuilt upon.

title: Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn drops coal from its timetable
summary: Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn prints its spring timetable with Slighe a' Ghuail's name shortened to an t-slighe, the line, with no coal in it. No order explains the change, and the drivers at Muileann chrom, the carriers and the farmers along the road go on calling it Slighe a' Ghuail as before.

title: Beathag marks the road's two names
summary: Reading the new timetable at an Leabharlann, Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh tells Sìleas nic Rath to mark the change beside the fuel's own spellings, saying a road keeps the name the men on it give it, not the name a board prints on a card.

title: Comann nan Gualadairean dissolves itself
summary: At its hall at Achadh dhomhain, in an Cèitean, the eleven masters left of Comann nan Gualadairean vote unanimously to dissolve the guild, out of a roll that had once numbered more than sixty. Its master Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh is charged with the disposal of its rolls, its sick-roll and its oath-stone.

title: Clach-mhionnan nan Gualadairean brought to an Leabharlann
summary: Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh brings the guild's rolls, its sick-roll and the oath-stone itself, worn smooth by two generations of thumbs, to an Leabharlann on a hired cart, and stands bare-headed in the rain through the whole of the unloading. Sìleas nic Rath, Beathag being away at Àth dhìreach, signs for the goods herself.

title: Tormod's letter copied into the record
summary: Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh gives Sìleas nic Rath a letter to be copied into an Leabharlann's record rather than filed among the guild's other papers, saying the guild had outlived the mountain's patience. Sìleas copies it that evening in a hand made to match Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh's own.

title: The bath-house passes to Deas-ghnàth a' Ghuail
summary: Among the guild's smaller goods the bath-house at Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh below Muileann ruadh, built for hewers whose chests the coal-dust had ruined, passes to the custodians of Deas-ghnàth a' Ghuail at the southern Seann Skell, the guild having named no other body fit to keep it.

title: The first Tuathach family bathed at Muileann ruadh
summary: In an Lùnastal a woman of Doire ghlas, brought south by her married daughter for a chest complaint, bathes at the springs below Muileann ruadh, the first Tuathach the house has ever taken in. The keeper shows her to the basin as she would show anyone and asks no leave of the custodians.

title: Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh returns to Seann Toll
summary: In am Faoilleach, against a doctor's plain advice, Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh travels once more to Sreath nan Gualadairean at Seann Toll to see how the removed families of Muileann dhearg fare in their first hard frost, though his chest has troubled him since the summer before.

title: Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh dies at Seann Toll
summary: Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh dies a little before dawn on the sixth of an Gearran, in a house of Sreath nan Gualadairean at Seann Toll, of a fever that settled on his chest. Gilleasbaig Ruadh sits with him through the two nights before the doctor can come, and the Row buries him themselves at the edge of the flood-plain.

title: Beathag enters Tormod's death herself
summary: Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh writes Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh's death into the day's page in her own hand, without asking her clerk to write it first, and sets beside the bare date his own line, that the guild had outlived the mountain's patience, and under it, smaller, that he had not.

title: Forty-one hands marked
summary: By the time her slip-box is full Sìleas nic Rath has marked in forty-one of the sixty hands that write regularly to an Leabharlann the month each first wrote of the fuel without the man's name.

title: Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh stands bareheaded at the handing-over
summary: The last master of Comann nan Gualadairean stands in the rain in the yard of an Leabharlann with his hat off through the whole unloading of the guild's goods, and asks no receipt but that it be said they came whole and not begged for.

title: The guild's oath above the pumps
summary: The buyer of the old hall of Comann nan Gualadairean at Achadh dhomhain leaves the lintel with the guild's oath cut into it where it is, above the dubhan pumps, since cutting it out would bring the front of the house down.

title: The sick of the springs under Deas-ghnàth a' Ghuail
summary: When Comann nan Gualadairean' bath-house at Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh of Muileann ruadh passes to Deas-ghnàth a' Ghuail, its custodians keep the old keeper on and take in the same sick, hewers' widows first, as the guild's rule had.
